metadata.note: Supplemental batch closing a gap: FC_001–100 contained no DUCS (Data Unit Calculation Sequence) questions despite DUCS being explicitly defined and repeatedly tested in the source Navigator OCR. All answers verified directly against source screenshot content, not inferred.

questions.question: What does the acronym DUCS stand for in OneStream?
questions.explanation: A is correct: DUCS stands for Data Unit Calculation Sequence — the series of steps that occurs when a Calculate or Consolidate step runs on one or more Data Units in a cube, running business rules and Member Formulas in a specific order. B, C, and D are incorrect — these are plausible-sounding expansions but do not match the term defined in OneStream training materials.

questions.question: What is the first step that occurs in the DUCS when a Calculate or Consolidate step runs?

options.C: Clear calculated data except for durable data
options.D: Run Business Rules 1 and 2 for the cube

questions.explanation: C is correct: the DUCS begins by clearing calculated data, excluding durable data, using the default Scenario properties. A is incorrect — the Scenario Member Formula runs as the second step, after clearing. B is incorrect — reverse translations occur after the Scenario Member Formula step. D is incorrect — business rules run later in the sequence, after clearing, the Scenario Member Formula, and reverse translations.

questions.question: Which step in the DUCS runs immediately after calculated data is cleared?

options.C: Run Business Rules 1 and 2 for the cube

questions.explanation: B is correct: after clearing calculated data (excluding durable data), the DUCS next runs the Scenario Member Formula. A is incorrect — reverse translations happen after the Scenario Member Formula step, not before it. C is incorrect — business rules run after reverse translations. D is incorrect — Member Formula Passes run later, after all business rule passes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of setting isDurableCalculatedData to True in an api.Data.Calculate function?

options.A: To automatically clear the data during the DUCS process
options.B: To ensure the data is always recalculated
options.C: To protect the data from being cleared during the Clear Data step of the DUCS
options.D: To remove all previously stored data in the cube

questions.explanation: C is correct: setting isDurableCalculatedData to True marks the calculated data as durable, so it is not wiped during the Clear Calculated Data step at the start of the DUCS. A is incorrect — durable data is explicitly excluded from clearing, not automatically cleared. B is incorrect — durable data persists rather than being forced to recalculate. D is incorrect — this setting protects specific calculated data, it does not remove stored data.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using Custom Calculate functions rather than relying on the DUCS?

options.A: Custom Calculate functions automatically handle tasks such as clearing previously calculated data
options.B: Custom Calculate functions allow calculations to run outside the DUCS, narrowing the calculation scope
options.C: Custom Calculate functions are only used for complex financial and account rules
options.D: Custom Calculate functions execute every calculation step each time they are run

questions.explanation: B is correct: Custom Calculate functions run outside the DUCS, allowing calculations to be more precise by targeting specific elements without executing the entire sequence. A is incorrect — Custom Calculate does NOT automatically clear prior data; a Clear Data Script must be added manually. C is incorrect — Custom Calculate is not restricted to complex rules only. D is incorrect — the opposite is true; Custom Calculate avoids running every DUCS step.

questions.question: Why might a consultant use Custom Calculate Finance Function Types?

options.A: To run calculations for every Data Unit in the cube
options.B: To ensure all calculated data is automatically cleared
options.C: To perform specific on-demand calculations outside of the DUCS
options.D: To simplify the overall calculation process

questions.explanation: C is correct: Custom Calculate functions are used to run calculations outside of the DUCS, enabling targeted, independent, on-demand processing. A is incorrect — Custom Calculate steps only process Data Units explicitly defined, not every Data Unit in the cube. B is incorrect — data is not automatically cleared; a Clear Data Script must be added deliberately. D is incorrect — Custom Calculate adds a configuration step rather than simplifying the process.

questions.subtopic: DUCS — Business Rules vs Member Formulas
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes where business rules can run relative to the DUCS?

options.A: Business rules can only run within the DUCS
options.B: A business rule configured with the Custom Calculate Finance Function Type can run outside the DUCS
options.C: Business rules can only be triggered from Cube Views
options.D: Business rules cannot be triggered by data management steps

questions.explanation: B is correct: a business rule written with the Custom Calculate Finance Function Type runs outside the DUCS via a Custom Calculate data management step, giving targeted, on-demand execution. A is incorrect — this is the common trap; business rules are not limited to running within the DUCS. C is incorrect — business rules can be triggered from Cube Views, data management steps, dashboard buttons, and Workflow Process steps. D is incorrect — data management steps are one of the standard ways to trigger a business rule.

questions.question: Why should a Clear Data Script be added at the beginning of every Custom Calculate rule?

options.A: To automatically save the calculated data
options.B: To ensure all previously calculated data is cleared before recalculating
options.C: To run all calculations within the DUCS process
options.D: To simplify the creation of business rules

questions.explanation: B is correct: because Custom Calculate steps run outside the DUCS, they do not benefit from the DUCS's automatic Clear Calculated Data step — a Clear Data Script (e.g., api.Data.ClearCalculatedData) must be added manually to avoid stale results. A is incorrect — clearing data is unrelated to saving. C is incorrect — Custom Calculate is specifically designed to run outside the DUCS. D is incorrect — this has no bearing on business rule creation.

questions.subtopic: DUCS — Custom Calculate vs Standard Calculations
questions.question: What is a key difference between how Data Units are defined for Custom Calculate steps versus standard DUCS-driven calculations?

options.B: Only Data Units explicitly defined will run, regardless of calculation status
options.C: All Data Units are processed regardless of their definition
options.D: Filters cannot be used for Entity, Consolidation, and Time dimensions

questions.explanation: B is correct: in Custom Calculate steps, only the Data Units explicitly defined in the step will run, regardless of Calculation Status. A is incorrect — standard DUCS-driven calculations use Calculation Status to determine what runs, but Custom Calculate ignores it entirely. C is incorrect — Custom Calculate does not process every Data Unit; only those explicitly defined. D is incorrect — Entity, Consolidation, and Time filters can still be used to define scope.

questions.subtopic: DUCS — When to Run Within the DUCS
questions.question: Why should Balance Sheet and Flow formulas typically run as part of the DUCS rather than as Custom Calculate rules?

options.A: To ensure calculations are unaffected by changes in dependent data
options.B: To ensure they are cleared and recalculated whenever there are changes in dependent data
options.C: To allow manual intervention in the calculation process
options.D: To enhance the visual performance of financial reports

questions.explanation: B is correct: running these formulas within the DUCS ensures they are automatically cleared and recalculated whenever dependent data changes, keeping Balance Sheet movement calculations accurate. A is incorrect — the goal is the opposite: staying responsive to dependent data changes. C is incorrect — the DUCS runs automatically, without manual intervention. D is incorrect — this relates to calculation accuracy, not report rendering performance.

questions.question: Which method is recommended for executing seeding rules when the source scenario data does NOT change frequently?

options.A: Using a Scenario Member Formula that runs within the DUCS
options.B: Using manual data entry for each period
options.C: Using a Custom Calculate rule that runs outside the DUCS

questions.explanation: C is correct: Custom Calculate is ideal for single or ad-hoc executions since it does not need to be reset and recalculated every time the DUCS runs, making it efficient when source data changes infrequently. A is incorrect — a Scenario Member Formula would rerun on every DUCS execution even when unnecessary. B is incorrect — manual entry is not a calculation method for seeding. D is incorrect — automated imports move data rather than calculate it.

questions.question: Which two statements correctly distinguish how Level 1 Data Unit dimensions and Account-Type dimensions are processed during the OneStream consolidation process? (Select 2.)

options.A: Level 1 Data Unit dimensions consolidate via the DUCS, applied to each relevant Data Unit
options.B: Account-Type dimensions consolidate via the DUCS, applied to each relevant Data Unit
options.C: Account-Type dimensions aggregate naturally through the account hierarchy
options.D: The View dimension is classified as part of both the Level 1 Data Unit and Account-Type Dimension categories

questions.explanation: A and C are correct: during the Consolidation Process, the DUCS is applied to each relevant Data Unit for the Level 1 Data Unit dimensions (Entity, Parent, Consolidation, Time), while Account-Type dimensions (Account, Flow, Origin, Intercompany, UD1–UD8) aggregate naturally through the account hierarchy rather than being driven by the DUCS. B is incorrect — Account-Type dimensions use Natural Aggregation, not the DUCS. D is incorrect — the View dimension is classified as neither a Level 1 Data Unit dimension nor an Account-Type dimension; it sits in its own 'Neither' category.

questions.question: Which of the following is dynamically calculated on-the-fly rather than stored in the database, under OneStream's default data storage behavior?

options.A: Base-level member data for the Account-Type dimensions
options.C: C#Share data, when the default Standard Consolidation Algorithm is used

questions.explanation: C is correct: when the default Standard (Calc-On-The-Fly Share and Hierarchy Elimination) Consolidation Algorithm is used, C#Share is calculated dynamically on-the-fly and is not stored in the relational database. A is incorrect — base-level Account-Type dimension data is stored. B is incorrect — C#Local is stored data, representing calculated local currency for input entity data. D is incorrect — YTD View dimension data is stored; it is the exception among View members, which are otherwise dynamically calculated.

questions.question: Is C#Top consolidation member data stored in the database by default?

options.A: Yes, C#Top is always stored regardless of the Consolidation Algorithm Type
options.B: No, C#Top is always dynamically calculated on-the-fly and not stored
options.C: C#Top is stored only when Force Consolidate is used
options.D: C#Top is stored only for Budget and Forecast Scenario Types

questions.explanation: B is correct: unlike C#Share, whose dynamic treatment depends on the Consolidation Algorithm Type in use, C#Top has no such condition — it is always dynamically calculated on-the-fly and excluded from stored consolidation dimension data. A is incorrect — C#Top is explicitly listed as an exception to stored data, not an inclusion. C is incorrect — Force Consolidate changes what gets recalculated, not whether C#Top is stored. D is incorrect — this storage behavior does not vary by Scenario Type.

questions.question: Which View dimension member is stored by default, while all other View members are calculated dynamically on-the-fly?
questions.explanation: B is correct: OneStream stores View dimension data at the YTD member by default; all other View members, including Periodic, QTD, and MTD, are derived dynamically from the stored YTD value when a report or calculation requests them. A is incorrect — Periodic is calculated dynamically from YTD, not stored. C is incorrect — QTD is likewise dynamically derived. D is incorrect — MTD is also dynamically derived, not stored.
